initial.prompt: Glaze original theme first material prototype, Rimebranch Tundra. Generate ONE pure standalone artwork on genuinely transparent alpha, NOT a contact sheet, mockup, widget, UI or wallpaper. A whole naturally recognizable winter rock ptarmigan bird in calm three-quarter side profile, round compact body, small rounded head, short dark icy beak, one visible round eye, two small sturdy bird feet planted together, folded wings and a short broad tail. A tiny separate arctic-willow sprig with three whole rounded leaves sits beside its feet. The entire bird and sprig are physically formed from INTERLOCKING GROWN HOARFROST ICE CRYSTALS: short rigid white needles and delicate fern-branched dendritic crystal fans, with dense milky-white crystalline cores, blue-gray facet shadows and a few thin translucent crystalline edge tips. Make the actual substance unmistakably crystalline ice rather than fur, feathers, wool, glass bubbles, moss, foam, porcelain, faceted stone or shredded paper. Crystals follow the coherent natural bird silhouette while still showing their straight prismatic needles and precise branching tips in a high-quality macro miniature photograph. Opaque crystalline body, no see-through hollow bird, no gold, no clock or numerals. Distinct quiet cool glacial whites with fine ice blue shadows; small mineral charcoal eye/beak give a readable familiar bird at icon scale. Whole subject centered with clean transparent space, focal group occupying only central 66 percent of square width and central 56 percent height; ample margin around every needle, foot, tail and leaf. Minimal isolated subject, studio macro lens, controlled soft top-left light, crisp relief and short dry crystalline shadows contained to the subject only. No snow floor, no landscape, no background color, no rectangle, no halo, no lettering, no frozen wreath or glass sphere. This is an original artist-made material interpretation of recognizable tundra nature, not scientific evidence.

selectedMaterialRefinement.prompt: Refine ONLY this same original Rimebranch Tundra ptarmigan material study. Keep the whole calm familiar ptarmigan bird, exactly two feet, small round eye/short beak, short broad tail and separate three-leaf willow sprig, the coherent pose, pure transparent alpha and clear exterior margins. The first image looks too much like a normal feathered bird with white fern-shaped icing on its feathers. Make the actual body and willow unmistakably a dry grown ICE CRYSTAL sculpture: show angular interlocking straight hexagonal hoarfrost needles and open miniature fern-branched crystal fans with bare rigid blue-clear prismatic edges and frosty opaque cores. Individual icy clusters are broad enough to read at small size, not fuzzy hair or repeating flat fern-leaf stamps. The folded wing is defined by short interlocked branching crystal clusters, not real feather layers. A few clearly straight faceted crystal tips break the contour while the entire bird remains smooth and recognizable overall. Cool white, gray and subtle pale-blue crystalline macro relief with tiny controlled ice highlights; no fur, cloth, feathers, foliage covering a bird, glitter, blue halo, fog, snow ground, glass sphere, paper, ceramic or background. Keep every crystalline tip and leaf whole, central two-thirds composition, soft controlled macro studio light. Transparent background.
